articles.title: WHAT WOULD A SERIOUS AI PRODUCT LOOK LIKE?
articles.summary: Current AI tools often act as misleading software. Serious AI products must feature error checking, robust citations, no first-person language, and non-natural language interfaces when appropriate.

articles.title: EXPERTS LEAD EXPERTS
articles.summary: AI is pushing leaders back into hands-on work, but that shift may be temporary. As building gets cheaper, expert leadership becomes more important.

articles.title: STOP MANAGING AI AGENTS LIKE SOFTWARE. START MANAGING THEM LIKE NEW HIRES
articles.summary: Organizations fail to deploy enterprise AI agents because they treat them like software rollouts rather than new hires needing onboarding and data prep. Clean data, workflow integration, and governance present far greater bottlenecks than model performance.

articles.title: GOOGLE HAS THE BEST AI MONEY CAN BUY. ITS PRODUCTS STILL FEEL BROKEN
articles.summary: Google's search quality failures stem from product and organizational flaws rather than model limitations. By layering probabilistic AI features onto a deterministic search interface without updating UI promises or user feedback loops, companies risk eroding user trust through unverified AI outputs.

articles.summary: The AI building boom risks producing generic "zombie UI" if teams ignore intent and artistry. To counter this, teams must maintain a strong design POV, encode standards into production, refuse to settle for standard builds, and invent new interfaces with AI.

articles.title: EVERYONE SHOULD PUBLISH THE DEEPEST, MOST DIRECT COMPETITIVE EVALS THEY CAN
articles.summary: B2B AI vendors should publish deep, direct, and continuous competitive evaluations against named competitors to build buyer trust, as demonstrated by Gorgias open-sourcing a live evaluation harness across 18 vendors.

articles.title: VALUE ACCRUAL FLYWHEEL
